A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCCE research work despite the revised title and organization. All 16 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular optimization experiments, model comparisons in Table 1, output-distribution analyses, and training and co-evolution curves.

after.justification: v2 retains original molecular experiments and adds baseline comparisons, ablations, docking results, combinatorial optimization results, and resource analyses.

M1.justification: The alternating frozen/local models, DPO objective, similarity bands, and fallback pair construction are retained. Appendix A9 newly details elite/Pareto population selection, while Table 9 specifies task-dependent similarities already allowed by the framework. These additions document implementation and instantiation without establishing a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates five-objective molecular optimization initialized from ZINC. v2 retains this coverage and adds Circle Packing, multi-objective traveling salesman, and capacitated vehicle routing experiments, substantially broadening the represented domains and optimization requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds reported molecular comparisons with GB-GA, REINVENT, MoLLEO, GFlowNet, and DyMol alongside the retained internal comparisons. Table 2 adds GPT-4o plus Gemini as a two-API comparator. The new routing experiments evaluate Pymoo, AIDE, FunSearch, ReEvo, and AlphaEvolve; their earlier appearance as citations did not constitute these comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include initial-population versus final-top-10 docking, MOTSP with n=100, MOCVRP with n=100 and m=20, and packing with n=26 and 31. Table 2 introduces controlled sweeps of similarity quantiles, API/local allocation, and update intervals. The original molecular initialization and model identities remain unchanged; newly disclosed resource settings do not establish changes to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained evolution, output-distribution, and loss analyses, v2 adds similarity-strategy, call-allocation, update-frequency, and two-API ablations in Table 2. Figure 6 compares training with and without similarity filtering. Docking validation and appendix analyses of synthetic accessibility and computational cost address additional questions about evaluator dependence and practical usefulness.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes its stated aggregation from mean and standard deviation over ten runs to five runs, although the shared numerical entries remain unchanged. This is a definite reporting revision, but the PDFs do not explain whether it corrects the caption or reflects different runs. No new significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 values are retained, including MCCE Top1 fitness 4.35±0.17 and HV 0.847±0.138. New baseline rows show GFlowNet HV 0.871±0.288, exceeding MCCE. Extensive new ablation, docking, packing, routing, accessibility, and cost results are reported; Table 5 places MCCE first on MOCVRP but third on MOTSP. The former Top100 fitness, Top1 AUC, and Top100 AUC entries are omitted.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 3's formal preliminaries, including the expected-return objective, SFT loss, and GFlowNet probability and flow equations. The substantive MCCE equations and appendix DPO objective remain equivalent despite renumbering. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs for MCCE.

C1.justification: The abstract and three listed contributions retain hybrid co-evolution, experience-driven learning, mutual model benefits, and applicability beyond molecular design. The introduction adds an explicit fixed-budget qualification to the performance claim. The additional cross-domain experiments principally support extensibility already claimed in v1 rather than redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of docking as evidence against exploiting a single predictor, including the GSK3β trade-off. Appendices newly argue practical synthesizability, cost efficiency, and transferable similarity mechanisms. A limitations section identifies primarily molecular validation and leaves continuous and mixed-variable settings for future work. Some interpretations exceed the evidence, notably treating favorable SA scores as proof of a hard constraint.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a concrete code-repository address instead of only asserting anonymous code/data availability. New documentation includes a 5,000-candidate budget, 50/32 API/local configuration, eight A800 40GB GPUs, runtime and API costs, TDC/RDKit scoring information, task representations and normalization, and detailed 50% elite/50% Pareto selection with duplicate removal. These substantially expand implementation disclosure.

R1.justification: The collaboration discussion now acknowledges training-based prior systems, including CollabLLM, trained small-model orchestration, and Collab-RAG. It refines MCCE's positioning around shared-task co-evolution versus one-sided or function-specific adaptation. Additional molecular optimization, combinatorial benchmarking, and synthetic-accessibility literature broadens the research context; renamed references to the same works are not separate additions.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, moves related work after experiments, removes the preliminary section, rewrites the main-results discussion and conclusion, and adds limitations and expanded appendix explanations. Separate ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage sections disappear, while impact and acknowledgements sections appear. The restructuring also introduces unresolved 'Table ??' references and retains a now-incorrect Section 4.3 pointer.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column formatting, with extensive figure relocation and resizing. Table 1 is reorganized into internal and external comparisons with fewer metric columns. Eight additional tables and a new two-panel stability figure are introduced, and algorithms gain numbered formatting. Existing Figures 1–5 largely retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's reliance on internal comparisons through external molecular baselines, targeted ablations, and orthogonal docking validation. Selection and resource documentation also materially improve auditability. These gains outweigh important unresolved weaknesses: unchanged results are relabeled from ten to five runs, several new baselines exceed MCCE's HV despite broad superiority claims, and the circle-packing score is not clearly reconciled with its stated objective.
